input.details: Employee E1003 ([NAME:E1003]) asked why her latest pay looked short for a Sunday shift. Pay statement PS-E1003-20261011, period 28 Sep–11 Oct 2026, paid Wed 14 Oct. Base rate $32.00. Timecard Sun 4 Oct 2026: rostered 07:00-15:00, punches 06:58-15:03, 30 min unpaid break, 7.5 paid hours, coded ORD (Ordinary hours). Manual edit note: punches entered manually by timekeeper on 6 Oct (time clock offline). Manager approved 12 Oct 08:30 (before the 10:00 cutoff). Under the EA, Sunday should be 175%: expected 7.5 h × $32.00 × 1.75 = $420.00; paid 7.5 h × $32.00 = $240.00; shortfall $180.00 (7.5 × 32 × 0.75). The ORD line of 45 h includes these 7.5 h; the correct split would be ORD 37.5 h + SUN 7.5 h. All other days check out: ORD Thu 1, Fri 2, Wed 7, Thu 8, Fri 9 Oct; SAT 150% Sat 3 and Sat 10 Oct (15 h × $48.00 = $720.00). Super on this statement was 12% of gross ($259.20), so super may also need adjusting (12% × $180.00 = $21.60) if penalties count as OTE. Please correct and back-pay.

text:
Thanks, [NAME:E1003]. You're right, your Sunday shift was underpaid by $180.00.

Your Sunday shift on Sun 4 Oct (7:00–15:00, 7.5 paid hours) was paid at the ordinary weekday rate instead of the Sunday rate of 175%:

- What you should have got: 7.5 h × $32.00 × 1.75 = $420.00
- What you got: 7.5 h × $32.00 = $240.00
- Shortfall: $180.00

Your timecard shows the clock was offline that day, so a timekeeper entered your punches by hand on Tue 6 Oct. The shift ended up with the wrong pay code. Your manager approved it on time, so this isn't a late-approval issue.

The rest of your pay (28 Sep–11 Oct, paid Wed 14 Oct) is correct:

- Weekday shifts: Thu 1, Fri 2, Wed 7, Thu 8 and Fri 9 Oct were paid at the ordinary rate.
- Saturday shifts: Sat 3 and Sat 10 Oct were paid at 150%: 15 h × $48.00 = $720.00.

I've passed this to a payroll officer to fix and back-pay you. Your ticket number is 10001, and they'll contact you within 1 business day. I've also asked them to check whether your super needs topping up for the missing amount.
